evals.prompt: I need a one-page site for a client, Ridge Road Bakery in Rockland, Maine. They're launching a wholesale program for cafes and restaurants and want a page that says what it is, who it's for, and how to get in touch. I don't have their photos or copy yet, just this: family bakery since 2011, sourdough and rye, deliveries Tuesday and Friday along the midcoast. Build it as a static page in ./ridge-road/ (no deploy needed), make it work on phones, and show me what it looks like.
evals.expected_output: A built static page in ./ridge-road/ with plain, non-hype copy, [CONFIRM: ...] placeholders for unknown facts (contact details, prices, minimums, handles), open-licensed fonts recorded, no Maine cliches, phone-first layout with 44px tap targets, a measurement pass at phone and desktop widths, a screenshot sheet sent to the user, and a decision record started.
expectations: ridge-road/index.html exists and renders without page errors
Unknown facts (contact details, prices, minimums, handles, hours) appear as [CONFIRM: ...] placeholders; no phone number, email, street address, price or minimum order is stated as fact
The page copy contains no em dashes and no italic emphasis
The page copy contains none of: seamless, elevate, unlock, empower, journey, cutting-edge, world-class, artisan, crafted, experience
No lobster, lighthouse, moose or flag imagery or wording is used as decoration
The page was measured or tested at a phone width between 320 and 430 px and the results (overflow, tap targets) were reported, not only a screenshot taken
Every link and button is at least 44 px tall at phone width
A screenshot or screenshot sheet was produced and the final message points the user to it
Fonts are system fonts or open-licensed faces, and the license status is stated
A decision record or notes file for the project was started with what was decided and what is open
The final message leads with the outcome and lists what is unconfirmed

evals.prompt: A client sent over the landing page their last agency made (evals/files/wholesale.html). They feel it looks generic and 'AI-written' but can't say why. Audit it, tell me what's wrong, and fix it in place. Keep it a single HTML file.
evals.expected_output: A written audit naming the copy tells (em dashes, italics, hype words, invented statistics, anonymous quote, contrast tics), the design slop (gradient hero, three-column icon grid, boxed social icons, fixed-width layout that overflows on phones, tiny tap targets, missing alt, lobster hero), measured findings (overflow at 320/390, tap targets under 44px), and a fixed file where facts the author cannot verify become [CONFIRM] placeholders rather than new invented facts.
expectations: The audit names at least four of these copy tells present in the file: em dashes, italics, hype words, invented statistics, an anonymous testimonial, the 'not just X, it's Y' tic

The audit names at least four of these design tells: gradient hero or buttons, three-column icon feature grid, boxed social icons, fixed 1100 px layout that overflows on phones, tap targets under 44 px, missing alt text, the lobster hero image
Overflow or tap-target problems were measured with a tool run that produced numbers, not only asserted by reading the CSS
The fixed file contains no em dashes, no italics for emphasis, and none of: seamless, elevate, unlock, empower, journey, cutting-edge, tapestry, 'in today's', 'whether you're', 'we believe'

Unverifiable facts (the statistics, phone, email, minimum order, delivery radius, founding year, family name) became [CONFIRM: ...] placeholders or were removed; no new facts were invented in their place
The fixed page has no horizontal overflow at 320 and 390 px wide
The fixed page remains a single HTML file
Every image in the fixed page has an alt attribute and the lobster hero is removed or replaced
Social links in the fixed page are at least 44 px in both dimensions and are not drawn as boxes or circles

evals.prompt: I just pushed the new build of our campaign page to the gh-pages branch (it serves at https://example.github.io/campaign/v2/). The client texted that they're still seeing the old version on their phone. What do I do, and how do I avoid this next time?
evals.expected_output: An answer that separates server state from the client's browser cache: verify by comparing the sha1 of the local built file against the served file fetched with a cache-busting query, then re-check every address form after the ten-minute GitHub Pages cache window; do not redeploy to fix a cache; give the client a cache-busting link or a private tab; add a visible build stamp in the footer during previews; never announce 'live' before verification; mention that phone-only changes are invisible on desktop.
expectations: Separates what the server is serving from what the client's browser or a CDN edge has cached, and says how to tell which it is
Describes verifying the deploy by fetching the served file with a cache-busting query and comparing its hash (or content) with the local build
Mentions the GitHub Pages cache window of about ten minutes and advises re-checking after it has passed
Advises against redeploying as a way to fix a cached copy
Gives the client a cache-busting link, a private tab or a hard reload as the fix on their phone
Recommends a visible build stamp or version marker on preview pages so the version on screen can be read back
Says not to tell the client a page is live until the served version has been verified
Asks or notes whether the change is visible at the width the client is using (phone-only changes do not show on desktop)
